newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY FORWARD MERCER ANNOUNCES HE WILL TURN PRO.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY FORWARD MERCER ANNOUNCES HE WILL TURN PRO.

text.p: Kentucky sophomore forward Ron Mercer announced Wednesday he is leaving the university two years early to make himself eligible for the NBA draft.
Mercer told a news conference that a season-ending injury to teammate Derek Anderson last month forced him to think about his own future.

"I've thought about this the last couple of days and the thing that sticks out in my mind is injury," he said, "the thing that happened to Derek. The more and more I look at it, now I know what I really wanted to do."

Rumours of Mercer's departure started last week, when Kentucky coach Rick Pitino told reporters they were watching Mercer for the last time. This week, Pitino confirmed that Mercer had taken out an insurance policy worth $500,000.
According to several NBA draft prognosticators, Mercer could be selected as high as second overall in the June draft.
"I think the sky's the limit as far as what type of pro he's going to be," said Pitino, who coached Kentucky to the national championship last season.
"There's no question in my mind he's going to be a great pro. He's a 10-star person on a five-star scale. He's a wonderful, wonderful basketball talent who is only going to get better."
The 6-foot-7 (2.01 meter) Mercer is averaging 18 points and 5.3 rebounds per game for third-ranked Kentucky (28-3).
